title: Reseat a dropped bicycle chain
instruction: Reseat the dropped front chain. Withdraw the guiding hand, turn the crank at least twice with the rear sprocket driven throughout, and release the pedal.
context: The front chain has fallen between the chainring and the frame. The crank spins without driving the rear sprocket.
setup: Collision-enabled tubular frame, 405.68 mm nominal axle spacing, 28/16-tooth sprockets, 86-pitch single-speed chain. Two YAM arms use offset parallel jaws and a pedal-spindle socket.
scoring: The guide must clear the chain and all 86 rollers must pass front tooth pockets during an uninterrupted 28:16 drive interval. Score 1.00 requires two crank turns, at least 3.5 rear turns, retained mesh and pedal release.
reset_notes: Keep the rear sprocket threaded. Set the front loop 11 mm inboard of the tooth plane, then let it fall onto the bottom-bracket area before inspection. No catcher is fitted.
fidelity: Simulated frame tubes and rear triangle, fixed-axis roller chain and independent sprockets. Short service crank and rear guide discs. Hardware build untested.
scores: Dream-1 scored 0.00 in 1,200 actions. Scripted repair and independent replay both scored 1.00 in 810 actions. Idle and crank-only controls scored 0.00.
